desk.period: First quarter of the six-month transition period (quarter to 30 Sep 2026)
desk.headline: Sales up 7% to $6.1bn, but adjusted EPS of $0.95 just missed; transition-period EPS outlook cut on energy and freight costs
results: Net sales rose 7% to $6.1bn, but most of the gain came from passing on about $435m of higher raw-material costs; volumes grew about 1%.
Adjusted EPS slipped to $0.95 from $0.97, a cent below the $0.96 estimate; GAAP diluted EPS fell to $0.52 from $0.57.
Flexibles sales rose 10% to $3.4bn with EBIT up 1%; Rigids sales rose 3% to $2.8bn with EBIT down 3%, partly due to businesses sold.
Free cash outflow widened to $820m as resin-price swings linked to the Middle East conflict tied up working capital; net debt rose to $14.0bn.
Dividend raised slightly to 66.0 US cents a share (65.0 cents a year ago, split-adjusted).

guidance.summary: Amcor cut its adjusted EPS outlook for the six months to December 2026 to $1.70–1.80 from $1.80–1.90, blaming the timing of passing on higher energy and distribution costs. It now expects leverage of about 3.6x at year-end, the top of its earlier 3.5–3.6x range.

points: Energy and distribution costs jumped late in the quarter, especially in September; management said about half of the extra cost is already offset and price and productivity actions should cover the rest by the end of 2026.
The CEO said these higher costs should not affect 2027 results, and the 2027 framework of double-digit EPS growth was kept.
Berry Global merger savings were on plan at about $60m for the quarter, and the three-year $650m target was repeated.
Volumes have improved for four quarters in a row; China is now a business of over $1bn and is getting new capacity.
The sale of the North American beverage business is taking longer than expected; the cash tied up in working capital is now expected back in 2027.
call.source: Coverage of the 4 Nov 2026 call: Packaging Dive (5 Nov 2026) and Earnings Whispers via Finviz (4 Nov 2026)

watch: Whether price increases recover the energy and freight costs by year-end as promised.
Cash flow and debt: whether the working-capital build reverses and leverage stays near 3.6x.
Progress on selling the North American beverage business.
